name: ifn-resistance
title: Type-I IFN field & cellular resistance

purpose.question:
Layered on the validated Increment-2 virus field + infection transition:
does a diffusing type-I IFN field, converted per-cell into a resistance
scalar (source formula `resist = f_bar/(a_rf+f_bar)`), gate an infected
cell's virus secretion by `(1-resist)` strongly enough to measurably
REDUCE infection spread and total virus versus the same run with no IFN
(Increment 2's path, unchanged)?

report.title: Increment 3: IFN-driven per-cell resistance substantially cuts virus load (primary evidence), with a smaller, later-emerging reduction in infected-cell spread — mechanism validated, reproduction still PENDING
report.objective: Drive `run.run_virus_infection_with_ifn` (Task 3.3) — the same 0.3mm/900-cell sheet, seed, and stochastic H->I transition as Increment 2's `run_virus_infection`, but with a second diffusing type-I IFN field wired alongside the virus field, and, each update, every currently- infected cell's virus secretion throttled by `(1 - resist)` where `resist = cell_resistance(f_bar, a_rf)` from that cell's locally-sampled mean IFN — and compare against `run_virus_infection` (no IFN, no resistance) run with identical parameters, to measure whether the IFN->resistance gate reduces spread and virus load (Task 3.3's integration test, `test_ifn_resistance_slows_spread_vs_no_ifn`, plus the fuller with/without series recorded in Task 3.3's report).
report.conclusion: MECHANISM VALIDATED, REPRODUCTION NOT YET ATTEMPTED. Same seed (17), same 0.3mm/900-cell sheet, same init_infected_frac (0.05, 45 of 900 cells seeded infected). The PRIMARY quantitative evidence is total_virus: with the IFN->resistance gate active, total_virus is roughly HALVED at every sampled step (819.16 vs 1750.69 at step 20, a ~53% reduction at the step Task 3.3's integration test actually asserts; 1222.88 vs 2752.34 at step 30, ~56%; 1624.58 vs 3905.38 at step 40, ~58%) — a robust, consistent signal from the earliest sampled step onward. n_I is a WEAKER, corroborating directional signal at the tested step: 48 vs 50 at step 20 is only a ~4% reduction, not on its own strong evidence of slowed spread, but the gap widens over later steps as the virus-load reduction compounds — 51 vs 60 at step 30 (~15%), 53 vs 69 at step 40 (~23%). So: the gate's IMMEDIATE, well-supported effect is on virus load; its effect on infected-cell COUNT is real but small early and only becomes a meaningfully sized effect by step 40. mean_resist over currently-infected cells jumps to ~0.53 after the first update and plateaus in a narrow 0.55-0.57 band through step 40 (it does NOT ramp toward 1 as more IFN nominally accumulates) — virus release is throttled to roughly half (1-resist ≈ 0.44) from step 1 onward, a steady brake rather than a hard block, consistent with the total_virus reduction magnitude. This validates the MECHANISM (IFN accumulates -> per-cell resistance rises -> virus release is gated -> total virus drops substantially -> infected-cell growth slows, weakly at first and more clearly with time) — it is NOT a claim that any of Sego et al. 2022's Figs 3B/5/7 quantitative targets are met; that evaluation is deferred to Increment 9 (the capstone).
report.main_insight: A per-cell resistance scalar computed purely from each infected cell's OWN locally-sampled IFN (no explicit cell-cell signaling beyond field diffusion) is sufficient to cut total virus roughly in half from the earliest sampled step onward — that virus-load reduction is the robust, well-supported effect. Infected-cell count responds to the same mechanism but more slowly: the n_I gap is small at step 20 (~4%) and only widens to a clearly meaningful ~23% by step 40, because fewer infections have had time to compound into a visible count difference even though virus release is already substantially throttled. The protective effect is real, but it comes from resistance hitting a fast local steady state (~0.55) almost immediately, not from resistance climbing toward saturation (~1) as more IFN mass nominally accumulates in the field over time.
report.caveat: This is a mechanism-validation claim only, with three explicit open items carried to later increments, most importantly a calibration flag from Task 3.3 that stays visible rather than hidden: (1) APC-driven IFN amplification is entirely omitted here (global-compartment feedback, Increment 8) — this study's IFN comes only from directly-infected cells' own local secretion, which here is UNGATED basal release: the CC3D source also applies `(1-resist)` to IFN's OWN secretion (`sec_amount = (1-resist)*b_fi` in Type1InterferonSecretionSteppable), a negative feedback NOT modeled here — Increment 3 gates only virus release per plan scope. Its absence removes a brake on IFN, so the modeled resist plateau (below) runs somewhat HIGHER than a fully source-faithful version would; (2) resistance's role in cell death, the Allee effect, and IL-10 cross-talk are all later increments, not modeled here — resistance in this study gates only virus secretion (and, in the source but not here, IFN self-secretion); (3) OPEN CALIBRATION QUESTION (Increment 9): mean_resist plateaus at ~0.55, not ~1 — the steady-state local IFN concentration each infected cell reaches lands close to `a_rf` (8.5e-6) in magnitude (resist ≈ 0.55 means f_bar ≈ 1.2x a_rf) rather than far above it, which is plausible but a "suspiciously just-right" coincidence between two independently-derived constants (a_rf from the ODE-scale calibration; the field magnitude from a separate secretion/diffusion/decay derivation chain) that Task 3.3 flagged as worth cross-checking against the source's actual field magnitudes/resist trajectories, not resolved here. Reproduction verdict (Figs 3B/5/7) stays PENDING until Increment 9.

study_card.goal: Validate that per-cell resistance, computed from local type-I IFN and used to gate virus secretion by (1-resist), measurably reduces infection spread and total virus versus the Increment-2 no-resistance path — no reproduction claim.
study_card.mechanism: A second diffusing/decaying type-I IFN field (secreted by infected cells) is sampled locally per infected cell each update into `resist = f_bar/(a_rf+f_bar)` (source convention, NOT the paper's printed `1 - ...` form), which throttles that cell's NEXT update's virus secretion via `world.set_cell_secretion_scale(virus_fi, cid, 1-resist)` — the infection transition itself is unchanged from Increment 2.
study_card.why_before_next: Increment 4 (epithelial death/recovery) and later increments (chemokine/IL-10, macrophage/NK/CD8+ response) all build on a cell's resistance state; this study establishes that the resistance signal itself moves in the protective direction and has a real, measurable effect on spread before anything downstream depends on it.
study_card.expected_result: With the IFN->resistance gate active, total_virus stays substantially lower than the same-seed no-IFN run at every sampled step (the study's primary, robust quantitative evidence, ~53-58% reduction); n_I also grows more slowly, but only weakly so at the earliest tested step (~4% at step 20), strengthening to a clearly meaningful gap by step 40 (~23%) — a corroborating directional trend, not co-equal evidence with total_virus. mean_resist over infected cells is > 0 once IFN has accumulated (the gate is actually engaged, not a no-op).
study_card.main_expert_question: Is the ~0.55 resist plateau (rather than ramping toward the paper's implied stronger protection) a real feature of the source's constants, or a magnitude/convention issue that Increment 9's calibration pass needs to resolve before the capstone reproduction can be trusted?

question:
Does a diffusing type-I IFN field, converted per-cell into a resistance
scalar via the CC3D-source formula `resist = f_bar/(a_rf+f_bar)`, gate
infected cells' virus secretion by `(1-resist)` strongly enough to
measurably slow infection spread and reduce total virus versus the same
seed/parameters with no IFN (Increment 2's unmodified path)?
hypothesis:
Layered on the Increment-2 virus field + infection transition: a type-I
IFN field secreted by infected cells diffuses and decays; each infected
cell's locally-sampled mean IFN drives a per-cell resistance scalar that
throttles ITS OWN virus secretion for the next update. This should leave
n_I lower and total_virus substantially lower than an identical no-IFN
run at the same steps, while mean_resist stays strictly positive once IFN
has had time to accumulate.
objective:
Wire the type-I IFN field (Task 3.2, `viva_cpm_studies/influenza/fields.py`
`add_ifn_field`) and the pure per-cell resistance function (Task 3.3,
`viva_cpm_studies/influenza/resistance.py::cell_resistance`) into a new
driver, `run.run_virus_infection_with_ifn` (Task 3.3), alongside the
unmodified Increment-2 `run_virus_infection`, and compare their per-update
series (n_I, n_H, total_virus, plus `mean_resist` recorded only by the
with-IFN driver) at identical seed/parameters (Task 3.3's integration test
`tests/test_influenza_virus_infection.py::test_ifn_resistance_slows_spread_vs_no_ifn`
and the fuller with/without series in Task 3.3's report). A minimal
in-package figure (`viva_cpm_studies/influenza/viz.py::ifn_resistance_figure`,
Task 3.4) renders both series side by side plus the mean_resist trajectory.
description:
Increment 3 of the influenza-sego2022 capability ladder: adds ONE new
diffusible field (type-I IFN) and ONE new per-cell state computation
(resistance, from local IFN) that gates the Increment-2 virus-secretion
rate. No death/recovery, no Allee effect, no IL-10 cross-talk, no immune
cells, and no APC-driven global IFN amplification — those arrive in later
increments. The IFN field's diffusion/decay/secretion constants and the
resistance formula's `a_rf` constant are taken from the CC3D
ViralInfectionVTM source (see `viva_cpm_studies/influenza/params.yaml`'s
`ifn:` and `resistance:` blocks); the resistance formula matches the
source's stored convention (`resist = f_bar/(a_rf+f_bar)`, a plain
Hill/saturation function), NOT the paper's printed form
(`rho = 1 - f_bar'/(theta*a_f+f_bar')`) — every source consumer applies
`(1-resist_source)` wherever the paper's rho appears protectively, which
is exactly how `run_virus_infection_with_ifn` uses it.
claim:
A type-I IFN field, converted per-cell into a resistance scalar, gates
virus secretion and roughly halves total virus versus an identical
no-IFN run — the study's primary, robust evidence. Infected-cell count
moves the same protective direction but more weakly, becoming meaningful
only later in the run. This validates the mechanism only; it is not a
claim that Sego et al. 2022's quantitative figure targets are met, which
remains pending.
expected_behavior: With the IFN->resistance gate active, n_I at any given update is <= the same-seed no-IFN run's n_I at that update (spread does not outrun the unresisted path).
total_virus with the gate active is strictly less than the no-IFN run's total_virus at the same update, once IFN has had time to accumulate.
mean_resist over currently-infected cells is > 0 once IFN has accumulated (the gate is actually engaged, not a no-op returning resist=0 everywhere).

readouts.name: Infected cell count, with-IFN vs without (weak, widening signal)
readouts.description: `n_I` series from `run_virus_infection_with_ifn` vs `run_virus_infection` (same seed=17, patch_mm=0.3, init_infected_frac=0.05, mcs_per_update=10): 48/51/53 (with-IFN) vs 50/60/69 (without) at steps 20/30/40 — a WEAK signal at step 20 (only ~4% reduction, 2 cells), widening to ~15% at step 30 and ~23% at step 40 as the effect compounds. This is a corroborating directional readout, not the study's primary quantitative evidence (see total_virus below).

readouts.name: Total virus-field concentration, with-IFN vs without (primary quantitative evidence)
readouts.description: `total_virus` series over the same runs: 819.16/1222.88/1624.58 (with-IFN) vs 1750.69/2752.34/3905.38 (without) at steps 20/30/40 — roughly HALVED already at step 20 (~53% reduction, the step Task 3.3's integration test actually asserts) and staying in that ~53-58% regime through step 40. This is the study's PRIMARY, robust quantitative evidence for the mechanism's effect; n_I is a weaker signal at the tested step (see above).

readouts.name: Mean per-cell resistance over currently-infected cells
readouts.description: `mean_resist` series from `run_virus_infection_with_ifn` only (no no-IFN counterpart, since resistance doesn't exist without the IFN field): 0.0 at step 0 (no IFN yet), 0.5290 at step 1, 0.5543 at step 2, then plateauing in a 0.5555-0.5697 band from step 3 through step 40 — reaches its local steady state almost immediately and stays essentially flat rather than climbing toward 1. FLAGGED (see report caveat) as an open Increment-9 calibration/convention question, not hidden.

behavior_tests.name: IFN-gated resistance does not let spread outrun the no-IFN path (weak directional check)
behavior_tests.description:
WEAK, DIRECTIONAL check only, not the study's quantitative gate: `op:
le, value: 0` passes on ANY reduction, however small, so a PASS here
proves only that n_I did not get WORSE with the gate active — it does
NOT by itself establish a meaningful effect size. Measured at the step
Task 3.3's integration test actually asserts (step 20): with_ifn
n_I[-1]=48 <= without n_I[-1]=50, a reduction of only 2 cells (~4%) —
a genuinely weak signal at that step. The gap does widen at later
steps (51 vs 60 at step 30, ~15%; 53 vs 69 at step 40, ~23%, per Task
3.3's fuller report series), so the directional trend strengthens over
time, but the quantitative claim for THIS study rests on total_virus
(next test), not on this loose n_I criterion.

behavior_tests.name: IFN-gated virus release leaves strictly less total virus (primary quantitative gate)
behavior_tests.description:
This is the study's PRIMARY quantitative evidence for the mechanism's
effect. Pass criterion: total_virus at the run's final step with the
gate active must be strictly less than the same-seed no-IFN run's
total_virus at that step. Measured at step 20 (the step Task 3.3's
integration test actually asserts): with_ifn total_virus[-1]=819.16 <
without total_virus[-1]=1750.69 — a ~53% reduction, already
substantial at the earliest sampled step, not just a loose
any-reduction pass like the n_I check above. The reduction stays in
the ~53-58% regime through step 40 (1222.88 vs 2752.34 at step 30;
1624.58 vs 3905.38 at step 40).

behavior_tests.name: Resistance gate actually engages (mean_resist > 0)
behavior_tests.description:
Pass criterion: mean_resist over currently-infected cells must be > 0
by the run's final step (sanity that the gate is not a no-op).
Measured: mean_resist[-1] > 0 at step 20 (Task 3.3); the fuller series
shows mean_resist reaches ~0.53 after just the first update and
plateaus at ~0.55-0.57 through step 40 — well above 0, though it does
NOT climb toward 1 (see the FLAG in report.caveat).

findings.statement:
With the IFN->resistance gate active, infected-cell growth is
slightly slower than the identical no-IFN path, but the effect is
WEAK at step 20 (only ~4% reduction, 2 cells) — not on its own strong
evidence of slowed spread. The gap widens meaningfully by step 40
(~23%) as the effect compounds, so this is a corroborating
directional trend that strengthens over time, not the study's primary
quantitative evidence (that's total_virus, F-02) and not a strong
signal at the step the underlying integration test actually asserts.

evidence.from_test: IFN-gated virus release leaves strictly less total virus (primary quantitative gate)
evidence.observed: total_virus with-IFN 819.16/1222.88/1624.58 vs without 1750.69/2752.34/3905.38 at steps 20/30/40; ratio 0.42-0.47 across the three sampled steps

findings.statement:
This is the study's PRIMARY, robust quantitative evidence. Gating
each infected cell's virus secretion by (1-resist) cuts total virus
roughly in half already at step 20 (~53% reduction, the step the
underlying integration test actually asserts) and stays in the
~53-58%-reduction regime through step 40 — a substantial, sustained
brake on virus load that is the direct, measurable output of the
resistance mechanism, and a much stronger signal at the tested step
than the n_I check (F-01).

evidence.observed: mean_resist 0.0 (step 0) -> 0.5290 (step 1) -> 0.5543 (step 2) -> plateau 0.5555-0.5697 through step 40; never approaches 1

findings.statement:
The resistance gate engages immediately (not a no-op) and stays
substantially positive throughout, confirming the mechanism's
qualitative direction. It only PARTIALLY confirms the expected
behavior, though: resistance reaches a fast local steady state near
0.55 and stays essentially flat, rather than climbing toward
saturation (~1) as the naive expectation of "more IFN accumulates
over time -> more resistance" would suggest. This is flagged, not
hidden, as an Increment-9 calibration/convention open question (see
report.caveat and the standalone caveat item below).

conclusion:
MECHANISM VALIDATED, NOT REPRODUCED. The type-I IFN field drives a
per-cell resistance scalar that gates virus secretion and measurably
reduces total virus relative to the Increment-2 no-IFN path (same seed):
total_virus is the PRIMARY, robust quantitative evidence, roughly halved
at every sampled step (~53% at step 20, the step Task 3.3's integration
test actually asserts, through ~58% at step 40). n_I moves in the same
protective direction but is a WEAKER, corroborating signal at the tested
step (48 vs 50, ~4% at step 20), widening to a more meaningful ~23% by
step 40 (53 vs 69) as the effect compounds — n_I alone at step 20 is not
strong evidence of slowed spread. mean_resist confirms the gate engages
(>0 from step 1 onward) but plateaus at ~0.55 rather than ramping toward
1 — a flagged Increment-9 calibration/convention question, not resolved
here. This increment has no death/recovery, no Allee effect, no IL-10
cross-talk, no immune cells, and no APC-driven global IFN amplification,
and makes NO claim about matching any of Sego et al. 2022's Figs 3B/5/7
quantitative acceptance bands — that reproduction verdict is PENDING
until Increment 9 (the capstone).

regression_compatibility.basis: Reproduces Task 3.3's measured integration-test result and report series exactly (same driver, same seed, same params.yaml constants).

biological_validation.basis: This increment validates the MECHANISM (IFN accumulates -> per-cell resistance rises -> virus secretion is gated -> total virus load is substantially reduced, with a weaker, later-emerging reduction in infected-cell count) with a single seeded run, not a quantitative reproduction against any of Figs 3B/5/7. Death/recovery, the Allee effect, IL-10 cross-talk, immune cells, and APC-driven global IFN amplification don't exist yet. The resist plateau (~0.55, not ~1) is an OPEN magnitude/convention question for Increment 9 — do NOT read PENDING here as a passing or failing reproduction verdict; no reproduction claim is made until Increment 9.

explanatory_gain.basis: No alternative mechanism is being compared at this increment; deferred to later increments / the capstone where a reproduction comparison against the paper's figures becomes meaningful.

biological_summary:
Infected epithelial cells secrete type-I interferon (IFN) into a second
diffusing, decaying extracellular field (source-cited diffusion
coefficient, decay rate, and secretion constant, per
`viva_cpm_studies/influenza/params.yaml`'s `ifn:` block), layered on the
Increment-2 virus field. Each update, every currently-infected cell reads
its own locally-diffused mean IFN concentration and converts it into a
resistance scalar via the CC3D-source formula `resist =
f_bar/(a_rf+f_bar)` (params.yaml `resistance:` block; NOT the paper's
printed `1 - f_bar'/(theta*a_f+f_bar')` form — every source consumer
applies `(1-resist_source)` wherever the paper's rho appears
protectively, matched here). That resistance throttles the SAME cell's
own virus secretion for the next update by a factor of `(1-resist)`, so a
cell that has accumulated more local IFN releases proportionally less
virus. Measured against an identical no-IFN run (Increment 2's path,
unchanged), this produces a substantial, sustained brake on VIRUS LOAD —
total_virus is the study's primary, robust quantitative evidence, roughly
halved already at step 20 (~53%) and staying in that ~53-58%-reduction
regime through step 40. Infected-cell COUNT (n_I) moves in the same
protective direction but only weakly at step 20 (~4%, 48 vs 50 cells);
the reduction widens to a clearly meaningful ~23% by step 40 (53 vs 69)
as the virus-load reduction has more time to compound into fewer new
infections — a corroborating trend, not evidence as strong as
total_virus's. mean_resist itself reaches a fast
local steady state (~0.53-0.57) almost immediately rather than climbing
toward saturation — because the IFN field's fast decay and diffusion
drive each infected cell's local IFN to a quasi-steady concentration
within about one update, and that concentration happens to sit close to
(about 1.2x) the resistance formula's `a_rf` constant rather than far
above it. There is no cell death/recovery, no Allee effect, no IL-10
cross-talk, no immune cells (macrophages/NK/CD8+ T), and no APC-driven
global IFN amplification feedback yet — all later increments.
key_assumptions: APC-driven IFN amplification is entirely omitted — in this study, IFN comes only from directly-infected cells' own local secretion, not from the global ODE-compartment feedback loop the paper models (Increment 8). The measured protective effect here is therefore a LOWER bound on what a full model with amplification might show.

Resistance in this study ONLY gates virus secretion (via `set_cell_secretion_scale`). The source also uses resistance to modulate infected-cell death probability and the model's Allee-effect term, and IL-10 secretion cross-talks with it — none of that exists yet (later increments).

OPEN CALIBRATION QUESTION (flagged for Increment 9, not resolved here) -- mean_resist plateaus at ~0.55 (f_bar ≈ 1.2x a_rf), not climbing toward 1, because each infected cell's local IFN reaches a fast secretion/diffusion/decay steady state that happens to land close in magnitude to `a_rf` (8.5e-6) — a plausible but "suspiciously just right" coincidence between two independently-derived constants (Task 3.3's report). Worth cross-checking against the source's actual field magnitudes/resist trajectories before Increment 9 locks in a reproduction verdict.

Single seed (17) for both drivers (same two-RNG-stream convention as Increment 2) — the with/without comparison is a single-run demonstration of the mechanism's qualitative and approximate quantitative behavior, not a statistically characterized effect size across a systematic replicate sweep.

As in Increment 2, there is no live-demo process-bigraph composite for the WITH-IFN driver — `run_virus_infection_with_ifn` is a raw `cpm_core.World` loop (Task 3.3), not wrapped as a composite. The `conditions.baseline` entry below reuses the SAME Increment-2 live-demo composite (`viva_cpm_studies.composites.influenza.viral_infection`, no IFN/resistance wiring) purely so this study has a dashboard-loadable baseline; it is NOT the composite this study's readouts are measured from, and it does not reproduce the IFN mechanism. All readouts above come directly from `run.run_virus_infection_with_ifn` / `run.run_virus_infection`.

The with-IFN driver `run_virus_infection_with_ifn` is ~4-5x slower per step than `run_virus_infection` (two diffusing fields, IFN needing 40 vs virus's 5 stiff-diffusion substeps per MCS) — a performance note for Increment 9's longer/larger reproduction runs, not addressed here.

literature_anchors.model_observable: mean_resist over currently-infected cells (this study's `resist` field, `resistance.cell_resistance`) rises from 0.0 to ~0.53 after the first update and plateaus at ~0.55-0.57 through step 40; total_virus with the resulting (1-resist) gate is roughly halved vs the no-IFN path at steps 20/30/40 (819.16/1222.88/1624.58 vs 1750.69/2752.34/3905.38).
literature_anchors.source: CC3D ViralInfectionVTM source (Type1InterferonModelSteppable.update_resistance) via viva_cpm_studies/influenza/params.yaml resistance: block

The MAGNITUDE of the plateau (~0.55, not saturating toward 1) is an OPEN Increment-9 calibration question — flagged in report.caveat and key_assumptions, not resolved here. No acceptance-band comparison to a digitized figure yet.

literature_anchors.expectation: Sego et al. 2022's reproduction (Figs 3B/5/7) implicitly requires the IFN-resistance mechanism to be strong enough to shape infected/uninfected epithelial-cell trajectories at paper scale.
literature_anchors.model_observable: This study's with/without comparison shows the mechanism moves trajectories in the correct (protective) direction, with a robust, non-trivial magnitude on total_virus (roughly halved at every sampled step) but only a WEAK effect on n_I at the tested step (48 vs 50 at step 20, ~4%), widening to a more meaningful ~23% by step 40 (53 vs 69) — at 0.3mm/900-cell reduced scale, using source-cited constants throughout.
literature_anchors.status_in_workspace: Referenced QUALITATIVELY only — this study does not compare against the digitized Fig 3B/5/7 acceptance bands (viva_cpm_studies/influenza/targets/); that quantitative reproduction comparison is Increment 9's capstone, not attempted here.

simulation_set.name: ifn-resistance-baseline
simulation_set.description: Reference run for the study — variants below perturb this.

IFN-gated resistance does not let spread.notes: WEAK signal at the tested step: with_ifn n_I[-1]=48 <= without n_I[-1]=50 at step 20 (Task 3.3, test_ifn_resistance_slows_spread_vs_no_ifn), only ~4% reduction; gap widens to 51 vs 60 (~15%, step 30) and 53 vs 69 (~23%, step 40) per Task 3.3's report series. Corroborating directional trend, not this study's primary quantitative evidence (see total_virus below).

IFN-gated virus release leaves strictly.notes: PRIMARY quantitative evidence: with_ifn total_virus[-1]=819.16 < without total_virus[-1]=1750.69 at step 20, a ~53% reduction already at the tested step; stays in the ~53-58%-reduction regime through step 40 (1624.58 vs 3905.38)

Resistance gate actually engages (mean_r.notes: mean_resist[-1] > 0 at step 20 in the pytest assertion; the fuller report series shows 0.5290 at step 1, plateauing 0.5555-0.5697 through step 40 (does not ramp toward 1 — flagged as an Increment-9 calibration question)

biological_validation.basis: This increment validates the MECHANISM (IFN accumulates -> per-cell resistance rises -> virus secretion is gated -> total virus load is substantially reduced, with a weaker, later-emerging reduction in infected-cell count) with a single seeded run, not a quantitative reproduction against any of Figs 3B/5/7. Death/recovery, the Allee effect, IL-10 cross-talk, immune cells, and APC-driven global IFN amplification don't exist yet. The resist plateau (~0.55, not ~1) is an OPEN magnitude/convention question for Increment 9 — do NOT read PENDING here as a passing or failing reproduction verdict; no reproduction claim is made until Increment 9.

regression_compatibility.basis: Reproduces Task 3.3's measured integration-test result and report series exactly (same driver, same seed, same params.yaml constants).

explanatory_gain.basis: No alternative mechanism is being compared at this increment; deferred to later increments / the capstone where a reproduction comparison against the paper's figures becomes meaningful.

derived.insight:
With the IFN->resistance gate active, infected-cell growth is
slightly slower than the identical no-IFN path, but the effect is
WEAK at step 20 (only ~4% reduction, 2 cells) — not on its own strong
evidence of slowed spread. The gap widens meaningfully by step 40
(~23%) as the effect compounds, so this is a corroborating
directional trend that strengthens over time, not the study's primary
quantitative evidence (that's total_virus, F-02) and not a strong
signal at the step the underlying integration test actually asserts.

key_metrics.label: IFN-gated resistance does not let spread outrun the no-IFN path (weak directional check)
IFN-gated virus release leaves strictly less total virus (primary quantitative gate)
